problem: The working Kontor app depends on a local service and devnet execution. A judge opening GitHub Pages needs a short, dependable way to understand why a changed invoice invalidates an earlier payment instruction and then inspect genuine evidence. Existing screenshots are long full-page captures; scaling them down would hide the approval state and decisive blocked-payment result.
userImpact: A first-time visitor should understand the protected business outcome within a short self-paced walkthrough, operate it on a phone or keyboard, and distinguish local tour interactions from previously recorded Solana devnet transactions.
proposedChange: Build a separate static guided replay using the actual Kontor UI and its cream, forest and lime visual language. Open with a concise hook: An approved invoice changed. Can the old payment still go through? Use six navigable chapters: approve 1,000; apply a 200 credit; inspect expired approvals; test the obsolete 1,000 instruction and see it blocked; obtain two fresh approvals and confirm 800; inspect the recorded devnet evidence. Reuse the actual App through a read-only tour presentation boundary. Use causal guide actions such as Show Mara’s recorded approval and Show the credit result to advance frozen historical snapshots; retain Back, Next and chapter navigation. Hide live mutation controls and retain meaningful local invoice/evidence inspection. Six chapter groups may contain substates so both original and revised approvals are individually visible. Show the acting person and the result of each action; preserve both named approvals rather than implying a single click is dual approval. Use a compact guide outside the app content, with one heading, at most two explanatory sentences and progress. Clearly label Guided demo · Static replay and explain once that clicks send no transactions. Use the settled c3f46241-966e-4264-ac88-035ed095ca23 run from browser-recovery-export.json for chronology and receipts; filter its accumulated network proofs by scenario. Do not add a pending-recovery tangent. Offer real devnet transaction links, evidence JSON and source links at the conclusion. Manual progression is the default; omit video recording and autoplay for this bounded first release.
acceptanceCriteria: The landing view explains the invoice-change risk, offers Start guided demo and a secondary Inspect evidence link, and identifies the experience as a static replay using synthetic Test USD with no monetary value. No claim implies a click on GitHub Pages submitted or confirmed a transaction.

The walkthrough visibly covers the original 1,000 amount, two named original approvals, 200 credit, revised 800 amount, expiration of the original approvals, blocked obsolete 1,000 instruction with no Test USD moved, two fresh approvals, payment confirmation for 800, and recorded evidence. Both original and revised approval pairs remain distinguishable.

Each chapter has a short explanation and current progress. Causal guide actions, Back, Next, chapter selection and Restart deterministically restore coherent read-only snapshots. No network availability or wallet is needed. Live mutation controls are absent; remaining app controls have meaningful local inspection behavior. Guide action labels explicitly describe showing recorded events, never sending approvals or payments.

Use the actual current UI components or a faithful source-derived presentation of them. Preserve the invoice, approval route, changed-amount breakdown, expired approvals, control result and payment review. Do not substitute a generic slide deck or shrink a full desktop screenshot into unreadable mobile content.

At 390 px and desktop widths, the guide and primary action are readable without horizontal scrolling. The phone layout places the guide and payment review before the invoice. Tour controls never cover the app action, proof links, or focused element. Long identifiers wrap or sit in labeled disclosures.

All chapter controls and primary actions work with Tab, Shift+Tab and Enter/Space through semantic buttons/links. Visible focus, descriptive accessible names, aria-current for chapter progress and a polite scene-result announcement are present. Scene changes have deliberate focus behavior; payment modal keeps native focus containment and Escape behavior. No drag, hover, color, or animation alone conveys state.

Manual progression is the default and no automatic advance is needed. Honor prefers-reduced-motion with instant scene changes; any optional transitions remain brief and do not move focus or obscure content. Do not add a separate video production dependency for the initial release.

Evidence links and exports resolve under the GitHub Pages repository subpath. Use a single actual run for the displayed chronological story; evidence from separate runs must be labeled separately. Failed stale-payment proof is described as a rejected transaction, never successful settlement. Evidence text states devnet/test funds and the relevant prototype limitations.

Check the complete path at desktop and 390 px, keyboard-only navigation, reduced motion, Back/Restart/direct chapter consistency, zero live action submissions, evidence links/downloads, and deployed subpath loading. Source-aware integration verification is distinct from independent usability evaluation.
tradeoffs: This is a source-aware pre-build UX research proposal, not a browser EvaluationReport or a completed ABU-11/17 negotiation. The sourceFinding identifies the accompanying research assessment. Parent remains the sole control-plane writer.

Manual scene replay is less cinematic than video but more inspectable, accessible, quick to revisit, and compatible with a static public host. A recording can be added later if specifically needed for a submission.
A guide that automatically selects the next demo actor saves judge effort but must name that actor and preserve both separate approvals. It must not imply a production user can approve as two people.

Reusing app components offers fidelity but can introduce coupling; a separately isolated static entry is preferred. SDE must choose a safe implementation that cannot accidentally reach live mutations.

Current screenshots and source support the visual assessment; the proposal does not assert observed judge behavior or establish a usability score. Screenshots from different historical reviews may have different credit references and must not be blended as one recorded run.

Implementation stays in tour/ plus its builder script; parent owns package/build configuration. Preserve live source behavior. A rejected attempt moves no Test USD but may incur a Solana devnet transaction fee; do not call it fee-free.

Engineering exchange accepts a minimal read-only App presentation prop in src/App.tsx owned by SDE, with isolated wrapper/guide styles in tour/. This replaces source-derived duplicate controls and the original suggestion that live-looking app actions advance scenes. It preserves source-real UI while clearly separating navigation from execution.
